page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u0.c1m1.4xlarge is an x86_64 virtual instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It is provisioned with 16 dedicated virtual CPUs and 16.0 GB of memory, yielding a direct 1:1 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 1.0 GB per core. The server does not contain integrated graphics processing units, local instance storage, or complimentary public IPv4 addresses, relying entirely on network-attached block storage for persistence. Network interfaces operate at a baseline throughput of 3 Gbps.

The 1:1 ratio of compute threads to memory places this instance in a highly compute-centric configuration. While standard general-purpose servers allocate 4 GB per core, this instance prioritizes thread density over working memory footprint. For parallel workloads that do not consume large memory tables, this structure avoids paying for unutilized RAM capacity. However, memory-intensive services will experience paging or out-of-memory states under full concurrency.

Appropriate deployments include multi-threaded batch compilation, video and audio transcoding, stateless microservices, distributed build workers, continuous integration nodes, and high-concurrency web proxies that maintain small per-connection memory profiles.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.u0.c1m1.4xlarge is a compute-focused x86_64 instance operating under the KVM hypervisor. Equipped with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 16.0 GB of system memory, it features a 1:1 CPU-to-memory allocation yielding 1.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not feature bundled local storage or dedicated GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached disks for storage needs, with network interfaces rated at a 3 Gbps baseline. This configuration provides high multi-threaded compute density while eliminating expenditure on unneeded memory capacity. The primary tradeoff is the lean memory ceiling, which limits applicability for memory-heavy databases or caching layers. It is best suited for horizontally scaled stateless applications, continuous integration build jobs, media encoding, and computational tasks characterized by high thread counts and compact memory footprints.
